All options (A through E) agree on the decomposition formula $W(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)}) = \prod_{p \leq \infty} W_p(\phi_{\delta}^{(N)})$.

- For $p = \infty$: $W_\infty = i^{-\frac{\ell^{N-1}(\ell-1)}{2}}$.
- For finite $p \neq \ell$:

More precisely, in these types of problems involving $\ell^N$-th power free integers and such equations, it is a known result that $1 \le \operatorname{ord}_\ell(r), \operatorname{ord}_\ell(s), \operatorname{ord}_\ell(t) \le N$. Consequently, $w$ (being the minimum of valuations of $b'_N$ and $c'_N$, which are derived from $r,s,t$) satisfies $1 \le w \le N$.
